Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.

Found mainly in New Guinea, which family of forty-four species — the males famous for extravagant, elaborate plumage sprouting from their beaks, wings, tails, or heads — is confined largely to dense rainforest?
Bird-of-paradise are members of the family Paradisaeidae of the order Passeriformes.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
Director of Columbia's Center for Sustainable Development, which economist led the United Nations Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals?
Jeffrey Sachs (SAKS; born November 5, 1954) is an American economist and public policy analyst.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy but also misused as a euphoriant, this fixed-dose pill packs four different amphetamine salts into one tablet. What is its brand name?
Adderall: Drug mixture used mainly to treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
This Scottish physician shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for discovering penicillin, and in 1922 identified an enzyme in his own nasal discharge — who is he?
Alexander Fleming: Scottish physician and microbiologist (1881–1955)
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?
Known by the symbol Sb and mined chiefly from stibnite ore, which element has long been powdered into the cosmetic kohl and today hardens lead in car batteries?
Antimony: Chemical element with atomic number 51 (Sb)
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?
With six species native to Africa (and one also found in Arabia), these large Old World monkeys have dog-like muzzles and have existed for at least two million years — what are they called?

This steel-gray, brittle alkaline earth metal is found naturally only in combination with other elements, making up gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, and bonds so strongly to oxygen that extracting it is notoriously difficult — which element, atomic number 4?
Beryllium: Chemical element with atomic number 4 (Be)
Conceived for Pan Am as a jet two-and-a-half times the size of the 707, this wide-body, led by designer Joe Sutter, rolled out of the world's largest building in 1968 — which airliner is it?
Boeing 747: American wide-body four-engined jet long-range aircraft.

Branching from the windpipe at a landmark called the carina, these airway passages narrow progressively through several orders before losing cartilage support and changing name entirely — what are they called?
Bronchus: Airway in the respiratory tract.
Bearing distinctive fatty humps and used for milk, meat, and transport across deserts for millennia, which ungulate comes in a common one-humped form and a rarer two-humped form?
Its raw shell and seed are actually toxic until roasted or steamed, and the tropical American tree it grows on also yields a fleshy 'apple' — what is this familiar snack?
Cashew: Flowering plant in the family Anacardiaceae.
Beyond the resistance-measuring "bridge" that carries his name, this English inventor also gave us the stereoscope, the English concertina, and the Playfair cipher — who was he?
Charles Wheatstone: English physicist and inventor (1802–1875)

Unlike oysters and mussels, which attach to a surface, or scallops, which live near the bottom, this bivalve mollusk instead burrows into sand or mud on the sea floor — what is it, the namesake of a popular chowder?
Clam: Common name for several kinds of bivalve mollusc.
Greenish-brown above and off-white below, this migratory leaf warbler is named onomatopoeically for its simple two-note song — which bird?
Common chiffchaff: Small migratory passerine bird found in Europe, Asia and north Africa.
Which tart fruit ripens on trailing evergreen vines with dark pink flowers, turning from light green to red as it matures?
Cranberry: Group of plant species bearing edible fruit.
Originally developed as an antidepressant, this fast-acting SSRI was later approved to treat premature ejaculation and was sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2003 — what drug is it?
Dapoxetine: Medication used to treat premature ejaculation.
Marketed as Lanoxin, this centuries-old heart medication boosts contraction strength while slowing the heart rate, but can cause blurred vision and breast enlargement in excess — what is it?
Marked by itchy 1-2mm blisters on the palms and soles that clear in three to four weeks but often return, this form of dermatitis has no known cause — what is it?
Dyshidrosis: Inflammatory disease of the skin in humans.

Often tangled up with mood, temperament, and creativity, these neurophysiological states carry a degree of pleasure or displeasure — yet scientists still can't agree on a single definition. What are they?
Dubbed the 'father of geometry,' this ancient Greek mathematician's treatise Elements dominated the field for nearly two thousand years — who is he?
Found on birds and even some non-avian dinosaurs, this complex evolutionary structure aids flight, insulation and waterproofing, and gives its name to the study of plumology — what is it?
Also called vitamin B9, this essential nutrient the body can't make itself is vital for building DNA and RNA — which is why its synthetic form, folic acid, is added to fortified foods. What is it?
Folate: Vitamin B9; nutrient essential for DNA synthesis. Folate, also known as vitamin B9 and folacin, is one of the B vitamins.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.
Nicknamed the "silent thief of sight" because it steals vision slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma: Group of eye diseases related to poor retinal and nerve perfusion.
Known to the British as the Martlet, this American carrier-based fighter entered service in 1940 and remained the U.S. Navy's best fighter against the Mitsubishi Zero until mid-1943 — which aircraft?
Grumman F4F Wildcat: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane.
A 1930s-40s Hollywood star of films like Algiers, she also co-invented a radio guidance system during WWII — which glamorous on-screen inventor was she?
Hedy Lamarr: Austrian-American actress and inventor (1914–2000)
Introduced in 1948 by a French naturalist, this taxonomic tribe groups humans together with chimpanzees and bonobos, but excludes gorillas — which tribe?
Hominini: Tribe of mammals. The Hominini (hominins) form a taxonomic tribe of the subfamily Homininae (hominines).

When the thyroid gland churns out too much hormone, the result can be a racing heartbeat, heat intolerance, hand tremor and weight loss — and rarely, a life-threatening 'thyroid storm.' What is this condition?
Hyperthyroidism: Excessive production of thyroid hormone.
Covering patents, copyrights, trademarks, and trade secrets, this legal category of intangible creations first developed as a concept in 17th- and 18th-century England — what is it called?
Intellectual property: Ownership of creative expressions and processes.
Caused by a buildup of bilirubin, this condition turns the skin and eyes yellowish and affects an estimated 80% of newborns in their first week of life — what is it?
Jaundice: Abnormal yellowish skin colour caused by high level of bilirubin.
This genus of coniferous trees and shrubs in the cypress family includes a species that forms the world's highest-known forest, at 4,900 metres in the Himalayas — what is it called?

Nicknamed 'acid' and 'Lucy' and derived from the ergot fungus, this semisynthetic hallucinogen is so potent that 20 micrograms produces noticeable effects — yet no fatal human overdose has ever been documented — what is it?
Traditionally kept as an indoor watchdog, this small non-sporting dog breed hails from Tibet — which breed?
Lhasa Apso: Tibetan breed of dog. The Lhasa Apso ( LAH-sə AP-soh) is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Sold under the brand name Cozaar, this angiotensin receptor blocker treats high blood pressure while also protecting the kidneys in diabetic patients — what drug is it?
Losartan: Blood pressure medication. Losartan, sold under the brand name Cozaar among others, is a medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
This genus of some 32 to 57 deciduous tree and shrub species in the rose family includes the domesticated orchard fruit tree along with crab and wild varieties — what genus is it?
Malus: Flowering genus, rose family Rosaceae.

The largest trijet ever built, this American wide-body airliner first flew in January 1990 and entered service with Finnair that December, a stretched, winglet-equipped update of an earlier trijet — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-11: Wide body airliners developed from the DC-10.

This American climatologist pioneered techniques to pull climate signals from noisy data, building a famous reconstruction of the past thousand years' temperatures with two co-authors in 1998 — who is he?
Michael E. Mann: American physicist and climatologist. Michael Evan Mann (born 1965) is an American climatologist and geophysicist.
Discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and boasting the sixth-highest melting point of any element, this metal is mostly used in steel alloys — what is it?
Molybdenum: Chemical element with atomic number 42 (Mo)
In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature into healthy ones, and some cases progress into acute myeloid leukemia — what is it called?
Myelodysplastic syndrome: Diverse collection of blood-related cancers.
This 17th-century Dane was a pioneer of both anatomy and geology — he doubted that fossils "grew" in the ground — before becoming a Catholic bishop and being beatified by the Church. Who was he?
Nicolas Steno: Danish scientist and Catholic bishop (1638 – 1686)
This order of predatory flying insects includes dragonflies and damselflies, whose aquatic larvae are voracious carnivores capable of overpowering small fish and tadpoles — what is it called?
Odonata: Order of insects that includes the dragonflies and damselflies. The adults are superb aerial hunters and their legs are specialised for catching prey in flight.

Powered by NADH and FADH₂ handed off from glycolysis and the citric acid cycle, this mitochondrial pathway is how nearly all aerobic organisms produce ATP — far more efficiently than fermentation. What's it called?
Oxidative phosphorylation: Metabolic pathway. Oxidative phosphorylation uses these molecules and O2 to produce ATP, which is used throughout the cell whenever energy is needed.
The males of this pheasant-family bird are famed for piercing calls and extravagant plumage; its Asiatic, green, and Congo species span India to central Africa — what common name covers them all?
Peafowl: Group of large game birds.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive fear that persists more than six months and can trigger fainting in blood-or-injury cases — what is it?
Phobia: Anxiety disorder classified by a persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Downgraded from planet to dwarf in 2006 when astronomers adopted a new definition, this Kuiper belt object orbits beyond Neptune—what celestial body is it?
Pluto: Largest dwarf planet. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.

A Mediterranean shrub in the mint family, this plant bears fragrant, needle-like evergreen leaves and purple, white, pink, or blue flowers — and those leaves are a beloved cooking flavoring. What is it?
Rosemary: Species of plant. It has numerous cultivars, and its leaves are commonly used as a flavoring.
The second largest planet in the Solar System is a gas giant with an average radius roughly how many times that of Earth?
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest in the Solar System after Jupiter. It is a gas giant with an average radius about 9 times that of Earth.
Drawing on fields from anthropology to epidemiology, this scientific discipline studies everything from sexual development in puberty to gender identity and paraphilias — which field of study?
Sexology: Scientific study of human sexuality.
Brittle, translucent, and found in nature as the mineral halite, this 1:1 compound seasons your fries and de-ices your roads. What is it?
Sodium chloride: Chemical compound with formula NaCl.
Known for a synchronized aerial swarming display called murmuration, this glossy-plumed bird family includes talkative mynas as members — which birds?
Starling: Family of birds. The Sturnidae are named for the genus Sturnus, which in turn comes from the Latin word for starling, sturnus.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?
Sweet potato: Species of edible plant.
Famously nicknamed 'white ants,' these wood-munching eusocial insects are actually genetically closer to cockroaches than they are to true ants — what are they?
Termite: Social insects related to cockroaches.
He joined Apple in 1998 to run worldwide operations and stepped up to the top job in 2011 when Steve Jobs resigned — which executive now leads the company?
Estimated to date back to the end of the Jurassic period roughly 156 million years ago, this fungal genus includes several species of truffles prized as culinary delicacies — which genus?
Tuber (fungus): Genus of fungi. Tuber is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).

Nicknamed the 'vampire fish' for feeding on the blood of larger fish through their gills, this tiny Amazonian catfish is infamous for an alleged, rare habit of entering human body openings — what is it?
Vandellia cirrhosa: Species of ray-finned fish.
Named after the German city where it originated, this all-purpose gun dog breed was officially recognized in 1891 — what breed is it?
Weimaraner: German breed of dog. The Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Ranging from small shrubs to tree-like giants such as the Joshua tree, this North American desert plant genus relies on a specialized moth for pollination and is also called Adam's needle — what genus is it?
Yucca: Plant genus in the agave subfamily.
